frontier.hypothesis: The entire 6-diff residual collapses if reorg leaves the sprintf jal's delay slot EMPTY on the s10/base body - no RTL reordering and no allocation change required.
frontier.mechanism: The saves are lazy text emitted by mips.c immediately before the first def of each callee-saved register, and sched1 does not reorder block 0. With the delay slot unfilled, cc1 prints jal, then (reorder mode) sw $s1,0x34($sp) and move $s1,$zero, and the assembler pulls the save into the slot - giving target's sw-in-delay-slot / move-after-jal pair - while addiu $a0,$sp,0x10 stays at its RTL position before la $a1, which is also exactly target. Because the RTL order is untouched, Lp stays 16 and Lc stays 20 and the 15000/15000 allocno tie that already gives target's $s0/$s1 assignment survives. reorg currently fills the slot with insn 21 (addiu $a0,$sp,0x10) - the nearest length-4 eligible insn, since both la macros are length 8.
frontier.next_probe: (a) Read tmp/grind/func_80037A20/dumps/code6cac_c.dbr (generated this session, never read) to confirm first-hand which insn reorg selects for the sprintf jal delay slot and what it rejected. Hard constraint: any spelling that adds an insn is out, the body is already 33/33.

frontier.hypothesis: The (ptr after, zero after) body at sandbox 8 is a second usable chassis: it already has target's move $s1,$zero slot, target's sw $s1 delay slot and target's $s0/$s1 assignment with STRICT priority margin (21818 vs 20000), so its only defect is the la $s0 sinking past the sprintf jal.
frontier.mechanism: On that body the pointer's live length is only 11 (the la is after the call), which is why the pointer wins outright rather than by a tie. The strict margin means there is slack: the pointer could afford Lp up to 12 before losing (24/12 = 20000 == the counter's 30/15). Any lever that pulls the la one insn earlier without lengthening Lp beyond 12 lands target's la position on a body that already has everything else right.

frontier.hypothesis: Either Rp can be raised or Rc lowered by a spelling that does not change the 33 emitted instructions, which would relax the Lc >= 1.25*Lp bar enough for target's statement order to become reachable.
frontier.mechanism: The bar comes entirely from floor_log2(Rp)*Rp vs floor_log2(Rc)*Rc. Target's statement order (Lp ~ 17, Lc ~ 14) becomes reachable if floor_log2(Rc)*Rc <= 19, i.e. Rc <= 7 (from 10), or if floor_log2(Rp)*Rp >= 37, i.e. Rp >= 13 (from 8). flow.c weights each reference by loop_depth, so a reference moved into or out of the loop body counts double.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate, from the target instruction stream itself, whether any of the counter's ten weighted references can be attributed to a different pseudo without changing a byte - in particular whether the tail pair (sw $s1,gp_rel + addu $v0,$s1,$zero) can be carried by a pseudo that is coalesced onto $s1 in local-alloc rather than being references of the counter allocno.
